title: Efficient quantum simulation of unitary gates based on atomic ensembles
abstract: We develop a technique to perform efficient unitary time evolution of a general spin Hamiltonian based on the system with identical qubits, as naturally realized by permutation symmetric atomic ensembles. We employ Cartan decomposition method to the associated Hamiltonian Lie algebra and construct the symmetry adapted generators to implement unitary operator of the ensemble Hamiltonian. This enables the compact circuit representations of the system dynamics in terms of experimentally accessible collective spin operations and exploits the Dicke basis structure of the ensembles as an effective qudit representation. We benchmark Cartan based evolution against both exact time evolution and the Suzuki Trotter product formula. Our results show that the Cartan protocol accurately reproduces the operator dynamics, spin expectation values, and fluctuation observables with zero error that are substantially smaller than those obtained through Trotterization while maintaining an optimized circuit structure. In addition, scaling analysis with the ensemble size demonstrates that the Cartan error remains independent of the atom number while the corresponding Trotter error increases with the system size, highlighting the improved efficiency of the Cartan approach for a larger system size.
summary: This paper presents a novel, highly efficient quantum simulation technique for evolving spin Hamiltonians in atomic ensembles using the Cartan decomposition method. By leveraging the Lie algebraic structure, it constructs a quantum circuit that achieves near-zero error, which significantly outperforms the error scaling of traditional Suzuki-Trotter product formulas, especially for large numbers of atoms.
main_problem: Developing an efficient method for simulating the unitary time evolution of a general spin Hamiltonian in systems with collective spin symmetries.
main_result: The Cartan decomposition protocol achieves zero error in reproducing operator dynamics compared to the Suzuki-Trotter formula, whose error increases with system size.
method: The authors employ the Cartan decomposition method on the associated Hamiltonian Lie algebra to construct symmetry-adapted generators, allowing for an optimized, shallow quantum circuit representation of the time evolution.
model_or_system: The study focuses on permutation symmetric atomic ensembles (e.g., neutral atoms or BECs) whose dynamics are governed by collective spin operators. The Hamiltonian is a sum of these spin operators.
key_observables: Operator dynamics, spin expectation values, fluctuation observables, and the error ($\epsilon$) relative to exact time evolution.
important_parameters: Ensemble size ($N$), simulation time ($t$), and the comparison between Cartan error ($\epsilon_{	ext{Cartan}}$) and Trotter error ($\epsilon_{	ext{Trotter}}$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption for the zero error is that the generator set is complete and the optimization yields exact parameters; otherwise, the error is bounded by the difference between the full and decomposed Hamiltonian ($\Delta H$).
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate interacting ensemble systems and the Cartan decomposition method, showing the decomposition of the Lie algebra into $\mathfrak{l} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$. Figure 5 compares the error scaling of Cartan vs. Suzuki-Trotter methods with respect to time and size.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of unitary evolution simulation, then details the Lie-algebraic framework and the Cartan decomposition. It proceeds to apply this method to specific physical models (like two-ensemble squeezing) and concludes with a rigorous comparison of error bounds against standard Trotterization.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, theoretically grounded tool for quantum simulation in AMO platforms, offering a superior scaling advantage over standard Trotterization for large, interacting ensembles by exploiting underlying symmetries.
